searchText: We can pin a message with an EIP name under discussion, if its helpful Yeah pinning a message would help. My dear about naming it is that it will confuse people who may need to use the room for coordination beyond the EIP listed as the room name. Open to other comments though. I'm fine with a channel per breakout, pinned message to EIP, or topic updates. Keep in mind, that one can freely create, rename, delete channels in Discord so you *can* have ephemeral channels effectively. In another server I am in they have a whole set of channels that just rotate through usage so history is retained, but they can have per-question channels at any given point in time. May be overkill in this case. 🤷 Hmm, removing RLP from 2718 introduces the problem of potential replay attacks with legacy transactions. I *think* we can avoid it by just asserting that `6` and `9` is not a valid transaction type? Current transaction signatures sign a payload that starts with `6` (pre-EIP-155) or `9` (post-EIP-155) since that is the first byte of an RLP encoded transaction of length 6/9. So if you have a 2718 transaction where the first byte is the transaction type and the remaining bytes are the transaction payload, then you *may* end up with a signature overlap. I don't fully understand why is it a good idea allowing the translation to be transparent from old format to the wrapper format. The signature in that case only covers the inner payload. > allowing the translation to be transparent from old format to the wrapper format What do you mean? Currently, the translation from old format to new is *not* transparent. You have to take a step to actually convert. On the call it was explained it can happen transparently in the client, e.g. old transactions remain valid. Oh, old transactions remain valid only for client APIs, which is only a suggestion in the spec, not a requirement. This makes it so legacy signing tools (e.g., MetaMask) don't have to update. You mean `sendRawTransaction` or what exactly? Yeah, `sendRawTransaction`. Well that practically means the old transaction format remains valid? Not over devp2p or as part of a block (transaction merkle trie). If the signature does not extend beyond the payload, then the old format is valid, no matter what, if i understand it correctly. As one can freely wrap and unwrap without changing the signature. The issue I brought up above is that someone may have signed something 2 years ago like `[6, ...]` and once we introduce transaction type `6`, if we go with "no RLP encoding, just first byte is type" then `[6, ...]` may mean something different and that signature from 2 years ago may sign something valid and new. All transactions *except* type `0` **SHOULD** include the transaction type in the signature. Otherwise you have to deal with ensuring there is no overlap between types, which is a big motivation for the EIP in the first place. 🤔 I should strengthen the wording on that to say that the signed payload should include the transaction type *first*. Btw to avoid that overlap is why I had that weird idea for the first byte, see <#745077610685661265>. But I am just trying to understand all aspects better, and whether it is a good idea allowing this transition period of old transactions remaining valid. Hmm, which weird idea? I am generally against transition periods where we allow multiple formats of the same thing over the P2P protocol and in blocks if we can avoid it. In this case, I think we can avoid it pretty easily. The problem we face right now with introducing new transaction types (without 2718) is that you **MUST** ensure that there is no overlap in signed data with all other transaction types out there. This rapidly becomes a minefield for EIP authors. It also is a burden on client developers because they can't just switch on some number, they have to differentiate between each transaction type in some special way. Like "if it starts with a 6 that means it is either legacy transaction type or that new one that doesn't use RLP and to tell the difference we need to read it as RLP and then check to see if the 6th item is an RLP list or not." I'm thinking about making legacy transactions type 6 (pre EIP-155) and type 9 (post EIP-155). That may reduce client complexity a little bit (by making it easier to differentiate those two types without having to first decode everything), and it would protect us from future replay attacks for those type numbers.
